note.explanation: Safe operation means using digital platforms and devices in a way that protects you from harm and avoids unwanted issues. For example, use strong, unique passwords and avoid unknown links. Secure use adds protections such as two-factor authentication (2FA), avoiding public Wi-Fi for sensitive transactions, checking account activity, and backing up important data.
examples: A message asks for your password through an unfamiliar link. Do not click it; check who sent it and verify the request another way.
You need to check your bank account. Wait until you can use a secure, private network rather than public Wi-Fi.
note.checkAnswer: Use a strong, unique password and enable 2FA.
note.simple: Keep your accounts and information protected: use good passwords, be careful online, and keep a backup of important data.
note.checkQuestion: Name two ways to protect an online account.
note.title: Using Digital Platforms Safely and Securely
steps: Create a strong, unique password for each account.
Turn on Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) where it is available.
Do not click unknown links or download files from untrusted sources.
Avoid sensitive transactions on public Wi-Fi.
Check privacy settings and account activity regularly.
Back up important data to an external drive or a cloud storage service.
note.answer: Use a strong, unique password and enable 2FA.

written.text: Describe the steps you should take to ensure the safe operation of digital platforms and devices.
written.finalAnswer: Use strong, unique passwords; keep software updated; avoid unknown links and untrusted downloads; adjust privacy settings; avoid oversharing; use 2FA; avoid sensitive transactions on public Wi-Fi; watch for scams; review account activity; and back up important data.

rubric.why: Passwords and updates protect accounts and devices from security threats.
rubric.description: Give password and update practices.
rubric.how: Mention strong, unique passwords and regular software updates.

rubric.why: Unknown links and untrusted downloads may expose users to malware or theft of information.
rubric.description: Give safe link and download practices.
rubric.how: Advise avoiding unknown links and downloads from untrusted sources.

rubric.why: Privacy settings and careful sharing reduce exposure of personal information.
rubric.description: Explain how to protect personal information online.
rubric.how: Mention adjusting privacy settings and avoiding oversharing personal details.

rubric.why: Further protective steps help secure accounts and preserve information.
rubric.description: Give additional secure-use measures.
rubric.how: Mention at least two of 2FA, avoiding public Wi-Fi for sensitive transactions, watching for scams, reviewing account activity, or backing up data.

modelAnswer: Create strong, unique passwords for your accounts and keep your devices and applications up to date.
Avoid clicking unknown links or downloading files from untrusted sources because they could contain malware.
Check and adjust privacy settings, and avoid sharing personal details such as your home address, phone number, or school name.
Enable Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) to add another layer of account security.
Avoid accessing sensitive information, such as online banking, on public Wi-Fi; use a secure, private network instead.
Be skeptical of unsolicited requests for personal information and verify the source before responding.
Regularly review account activity and respond to suspicious activity by changing your password and reporting it to the platform.
Back up important data to an external hard drive or a cloud storage service.

explain.title: Safe operation
explain.body: Your textbook explains: “When we talk about the "safe operation" of digital platforms and devices, we mean using them in a way that protects you from harm and avoids any unwanted issues.” Use strong, unique passwords, keep software updated, be careful with links and downloads, check privacy settings, and avoid oversharing.

explain.title: Secure use and 2FA
explain.body: Your textbook explains: “Using digital platforms securely means taking extra steps to protect your information and ensuring that your online activities do not put you or others at risk.” 2FA asks for another piece of information after your password, such as a code sent to your phone.

explain.title: Public Wi-Fi and scams
explain.body: Public Wi-Fi is often less secure, so avoid sensitive transactions such as online banking while connected to it. Treat unexpected requests for personal information cautiously and verify the source before responding.

explain.title: Checking accounts and backing up data
explain.body: Review recent logins, messages, and transactions for unusual activity. If something looks suspicious, change your password and report it to the platform. Back up important data to an external hard drive or a cloud storage service.

mistakes: Using the same password for different accounts instead of creating strong, unique passwords.
Clicking an unfamiliar link or downloading a file before checking whether its source is trusted.
Using public Wi-Fi for sensitive transactions even though public networks are often less secure.
Sharing personal details such as a home address, phone number, or school name online.
Thinking that a password alone is the same as 2FA; 2FA requires another piece of information.
Ignoring unusual account activity instead of changing the password and reporting it to the platform.
